methodological_rigor.justification: This is a large multicenter real-world cohort (190 patients; 1,578 plasma samples) with longitudinal ctDNA testing using a tumor-informed assay and clinically annotated outcomes. The manuscript explicitly notes nonstandardized postoperative sampling and treatment decisions at physician discretion, which introduces selection and intervention confounding, but it also describes mitigation of guarantee-time bias by modeling ctDNA as a time-varying covariate in Cox analyses. Reported effect sizes are consistently large (e.g., anytime ctDNA positivity associated with shorter RFS with HR 40.63; 95% CI 19.9–82.96), and multivariable analysis compares ctDNA to clinicopathologic factors, supporting internal coherence despite the retrospective design.

clinical_relevance_loe.justification: The study is an individual retrospective cohort analysis, so Oxford LoE is 2b. Clinical relevance is high because ctDNA positivity preceded radiographic recurrence by a median of 3.3 months and was associated with major recurrence-risk stratification across stage I to IIIB disease. The work also documents that ctDNA results changed management in most ctDNA-positive patients (76.5%), including intensified imaging and occasional treatment initiation based on ctDNA alone, making the findings directly pertinent to postsurgical surveillance strategies.

reporting_quality.justification: For an observational real-world cohort, STROBE is appropriate, and the manuscript reports cohort size, stage distribution, sample counts, follow-up duration, and key outcomes with hazard ratios and confidence intervals. It is transparent about nonstandardized sampling (first postoperative draw range 0–60.83 months) and heterogeneity in adjuvant therapy and imaging, and it provides specific definitions (e.g., recurrence windows within 2 weeks) for the longitudinal analyses. No explicit public data/code deposition is provided in the normalized text, so reproducibility appears limited to the described methods.

novelty_literature.justification: ctDNA as a prognostic biomarker in melanoma has prior precedent, so the core concept is not first-in-class. The meaningful novelty here is the scale and breadth of a stage I–IIIB real-world dataset with repeated sampling and explicit examples of ctDNA-driven clinical actions, including 'treat-on-molecular recurrence' cases with subsequent ctDNA clearance. This positions the work as a substantial, practice-informing extension rather than a paradigm shift.

writing_presentation.justification: The manuscript is clearly structured, with a quantitative abstract (sample counts, follow-up, HRs with CIs) and consistent framing of postsurgical surveillance use cases. Key results are stated with concrete numbers (e.g., 24/33 ctDNA-positive around recurrence; median 3.3-month lead time) and limitations inherent to retrospective real-world design are discussed directly. Terminology such as post–definitive treatment surveillance and the linkage to management changes is explained in a way that supports interpretation.

key_strengths: Large, multicenter real-world cohort with dense longitudinal sampling (190 patients; 1,578 samples) enabling robust association testing.

Very strong and consistent prognostic signal for recurrence risk (anytime postoperative ctDNA positivity HR 40.63 for RFS) with multivariable analyses and time-varying modeling to mitigate guarantee-time bias.
Direct evidence of clinical utility via documented management changes after ctDNA positivity (e.g., intensified imaging and selected ctDNA-triggered treatment initiation).
key_concerns: Retrospective design with nonstandardized sampling (first postoperative draw varies widely) and physician-discretion interventions, which can confound observed associations and management-impact narratives.
Unclear generalizability of 'treat-on-molecular recurrence' scenarios given small counts (3 cases) and heterogeneous follow-up across institutions.
Lack of explicit data/code sharing in the provided manuscript limits independent reproducibility and external validation.
chief_reviewer.rationale: The work is a strong, clinically relevant real-world demonstration that longitudinal tumor-informed ctDNA is a powerful prognostic marker in resected stage I–IIIB melanoma, suitable for a tier-2 journal with modest clarifications around bias, standardization, and reproducibility.
